transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst.
Police in the United Kingdom say several people have been arrested overnight in connection
to explosive devices found near Fairford.
That's a U.K. military base in southwest England that's used by U.S. service members for strikes
on Iran.
Assistant Chief Constable Richard O'Kone says police evacuated dozens of homes near the
base.
"As a precaution, around 85 households have been advised to evacuate while these examinations
take place."
And a bomb squad is there as armed officers reportedly guard the entrance.
The base has been the scene of protests over the British government's decision this summer
to allow the U.S. to use it for staging limited strikes on Iranian missile sites, but Iran
says bombers flying from the base have been used for strikes beyond the original usage
mandate.
Iran says that made the base a legitimate target in the ongoing U.S. war against Iran.
Diesel prices have slipped just a little, but the war in Iran continues to strain fuel
supplies.
NPR's Windsor Johnston reports the concern now is how long higher costs could keep working
their way into household bills.
Farmers in many parts of the country are still paying much more to run combines, tractors
and trucks during the fall harvest.
Higher fuel costs can move through the food supply chain, and the pressure may last.
Diesel and home heating oil draw on the same tight fuel supply as winter approaches.
Some shipping costs are set by contractors, so shoppers may not see the full effect right
away.
U.S. fuel inventories are low, leaving little cushion if supplies are disrupted again.
That's why a modest drop in diesel prices offers only limited relief.
The Trump administration has discussed expanding U.S. refining capacity but has not announced
an immediate measure to lower prices.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
A powerful nor'easter remains stalled off New York and New Jersey, pushing water into
coastal communities.
Coastal flood warnings remain in effect today.
NPR's Amy Held reports at least one storm-related death was reported in New York City.
In Brooklyn, a falling tree killed a worker for the New York Housing Authority.
As wind gusts topped 60 miles per hour, more than 100,000 power outages were reported from
the Mid-Atlantic to New England.
Some New Yorkers kayaked through flooded city streets.
At the Jersey Shore, some areas saw their highest flooding since Superstorm Sandy 14
years ago.
Anne Fitzsimmons, owner of Jay's On Third Restaurant in Stone Harbor, says she and her
team are doing their best to stay afloat.
"Everyone is here, all hands on deck, we're going to get cleaned up, we've been getting
rid of the water, we have fans running to dry it out."
Forecasters expect repeated rounds of coastal flooding as the system loops offshore before
moving out early in the week.
Amy Held, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The competition is fierce during Alaska's annual Fat Bear Week.
People around the world are casting their votes for their favorite bulky brown bear
at Katmai National Park and Preserve.
Alaska Public Media's Ava White has more.
As the brown bears continue fattening up on sockeye salmon, the original field of 16 chunky
competitors is thinning.
Katmai park ranger Sarah Bruce says, "Even if the plum participant you're rooting for
doesn't take the top spot as bad as bear, they're all still winners."
"The bears have no idea that this is happening.
They have already won in the fact that they are set to survive another winter hibernation."
Voting in the bracket style competition is closed over the weekend but reopens Monday.
Fat Bear Week ends Tuesday when a chubby champ will be crowned.
You can vote online at fatbearweek.org.
For NPR News, I'm Ava White in Anchorage.
Two giant pandas are on their way to the Atlanta Zoo, leaving Chengdu in southwestern China
early today.
In Washington last week, Chinese President Xi Jinping said the pandas would arrive in
the U.S. in the coming days.
The arrival of the pandas, which are on loan from China, is one of the few concrete outcomes
of that state visit.
Atlanta Zoo has been without pandas since 2024 when the last ones went back home.
And now, Pingping, a male, and Fuxuang, a female, both adults, will stay for 10 years.
They're both six years old.
The Panda Loan Program is part of China's Global Diplomacy Program.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now, sponsor free, through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Police arrest several people overnight in connection with explosive devices found near Fairford military base in UK
Diesel prices slip slightly but war in Iran continues to strain fuel supplies and household costs
Powerful nor'easter stalled off New York and New Jersey pushes water into coastal communities, killing at least one
Alaska's annual Fat Bear Week competition continues as brown bears fatten up on sockeye salmon at Katmai
Two giant pandas from China on their way to Atlanta Zoo for 10-year loan as part of diplomacy program
